truths.truth: The guard fails on each added tag with a file:line message, and allows 'phase 2' in markdown and UTF-16 in a Rust comment (AC4; criterion 2's 'fails when a source comment cites a planning tag')
truths.evidence: The built guard binary was run after each of these edits, one at a time. Each edit was restored byte- and mtime-exact before the next (cmp plus stat), and git status was identical before and after. P1: '// see SRCH-02' appended to crates/terminus-core/src/lib.rs gives exit 101, 'crates/terminus-core/src/lib.rs:53: SRCH-02'. P2: '// (D-04)' appended to crates/terminus/tests/cli.rs gives 'crates/terminus/tests/cli.rs:1548: D-04'. P3: '-- INJ-07' as a new line 62 inside CREATE_SQL gives 'crates/terminus-core/src/store/schema.rs:62: INJ-07'. P4: '# AC3' appended to fuzz/Cargo.toml gives 'fuzz/Cargo.toml:117: AC3'. P5: ING-08 on docs/json-shapes.md:3 gives 'docs/json-shapes.md:3: ING-08'. N1: 'phase 2' on docs/json-shapes.md:3 gives exit 0. N2: '// UTF-16 here' in lib.rs gives exit 0. Extra: '// lands in Phase 3' fails ('config.rs:1321: Phase 3'), and a trailing 'fn _probe() {} // RET-05' fails. The 10 matcher and extractor self-tests pass (planning_tags.rs:358-518). Known limits, all from D-14 and D-15 and none holding a tag today: block comments (the tree has none), a TOML comment after a value (none in the 4 manifests), a '--' after SQL text on a CREATE_SQL line (none), string literals such as assert! messages, markdown outside docs/ and tests/fixtures/README.md, and the Task N family (truth 3).

truths.truth: Outside the guard file, the phase's diff changes only comment lines, assert!/panic! message text and markdown prose (ROADMAP criterion 3 as D-06 reads it, AC5)
truths.evidence: Line check: git diff -U0 1c55fec 281ee53 over *.rs, excluding planning_tags.rs, has 46 changed lines that do not start with // or --. They are 23 -/+ pairs, each the message string of an assert!, assert_eq! or panic! at a site D-06 names: capture.rs, config.rs x3, derive.rs, discover.rs, fixtures.rs x2, ingest.rs x4, parse.rs, reindex.rs, store_open.rs, cli.rs x2, corpus.rs x2, crash.rs x3, mcp.rs. Token check: a comment-stripping lexer (scratchpad strip.py) drops //, block comments and the -- lines inside schema.rs strings, then compares the token stream of all 143 changed .rs files at 1c55fec and 281ee53. It finds exactly 23 differing tokens, each one of those message string literals, and no code token changed. All 121 changed -- lines are in schema.rs, at HEAD lines 66-376, inside CREATE_SQL (61-381). No CREATE_SQL line ends in a backslash, so no comment can swallow SQL. The TOML diff (Cargo.toml, crates/terminus/Cargo.toml) changes only # lines. Outside .planning, the only other files changed are docs/json-shapes.md and tests/fixtures/README.md: no test reads either, and the README's fixture filenames are identical before and after. e2ea721 touches only .planning. Side effect: the two message-only edits at crates/terminus-core/tests/reindex.rs:117 and crates/terminus/tests/cli.rs:472 leave rustfmt drift in two files that were clean, and cargo fmt --all -- --check now names 7 files. CI does not gate on rustfmt, and SUMMARY records the trade-off.

truths.truth: The guard fails rather than passes when it reads nothing: CREATE_SQL's declaration not found, or a root below its file floor
truths.evidence: Same restore-exact probe method as truth 5. F1: renaming 'pub const CREATE_SQL' to 'pub const SCHEMA_SQL' in schema.rs gives exit 101 at planning_tags.rs:329: 'only 0 SQL comment lines read from crates/terminus-core/src/store/schema.rs; is `pub const CREATE_SQL` still declared there?'. F2: moving the opening quote to the next line gives the same message. F3: moving fuzz/src/lib.rs aside gives exit 101 at planning_tags.rs:318: 'only 0 .rs files under fuzz/src'. The floors (planning_tags.rs:248-256, 271) sit below the current counts (53/36/35/27/13/1 .rs files, 15 docs .md, 157 CREATE_SQL comment lines). The declaration is matched with line.contains, so a rename that keeps the prefix (such as CREATE_SQL_V2) still counts as found, which is correct because its comments are still read.
